summary: Implicit role mapping disabled due to claim-whitelist filtering; service-account batch workers receiving 403 in private VPC
description: Issue summary: After onboarding AtlasFin Labs into a Private deployment (VPC), scheduled batch workers using a service account began receiving 403s when calling the Redwood Admin API. Root cause suspected to be RBAC role mapping not being applied because IdP assertion attributes were filtered by our claim-whitelist setting in the identity proxy. Impact: Multiple scheduled inference jobs failing, delayed SLAs for nightly batch runs. Scope: Affects service-account impersonation for batch workers only; interactive console access unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a service account in AtlasFin's IdP with role attribute urn:atlasfin:roles/service-admin (note the urn prefix).
2) Configure SCIM provisioning to emit attribute 'roles' but IdP sends claim name 'urn:atlasfin:roles' (namespaced).
3) Private identity-proxy is configured with claim_whitelist: [ 'roles', 'email', 'sub' ] (missing the urn-prefixed key).
4) Trigger a scheduled worker run which exchanges the IdP token for a Redwood service token and calls Admin API endpoints.
5) Observe Admin API responses: 403 Forbidden for operations requiring service-admin role; request log shows subject mapped without roles.
logs: 2026-03-11T22:03:12Z identity-proxy DEBUG: claim_whitelist applied -> allowed_claims=["roles","email","sub"] ; dropped_claims=["urn:atlasfin:roles"]
2026-03-11T22:03:12Z authz-service WARN: principal batcher@atlasfin.com has no mapped roles after claim normalization; returning 403
Admin API request id=abc123 status=403 user=batcher@atlasfin.com effective_roles=[]
investigation_notes: Customer reports batch runs started failing immediately after we enabled the identity-proxy claim_whitelist hardening change in private deployments on 2026-03-10.
Reproduced in a staging private cluster by simulating IdP that emits only urn-prefixed role attributes (common for this IdP).

Hypothesis: our claim_whitelist uses simple keys (roles) and normalization strips namespace prefixes, but we currently do not canonicalize urn-prefixed claims -> whitelistFiltering removes the attribute entirely.

Observed that SCIM-provisioned user has expected role binding in Redwood; but service-account flow uses assertion claims for short-lived tokens and relies on implicit role mapping, which is failing because the role claim is absent after proxy filtering.
Quick check: adding 'urn:atlasfin:roles' to whitelist in proxy restores role mapping and scheduled jobs succeed.
comments: Priya Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer noticed nightly job failures and opened the ticket after rotating proxy hardening flags.
Jordan Lee (Eng) 2026-03-12: Assigned. I'll validate normalization rules in identity-proxy and the implicit role-mapping path for token-exchange flows.

Jordan Lee (Eng) 2026-03-13: Confirmed reproduction in staging. Patch in branch fixes: normalize claim keys by removing common URN prefixes when evaluating whitelist and when mapping roles. Preparing PR and test cases.
Priya Patel (Support) 2026-03-14: Customer applied workaround and reported nightly jobs completed successfully last night. We'll schedule rollback once patch is rolled out.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Instructed customer to add their namespaced claim key ('urn:atlasfin:roles') to the identity-proxy claim_whitelist to restore roles. Permanent fix: engineering implemented normalization logic in identity-proxy so that common URN prefixes (e.g., urn:, http://schemas., https://schemas.) are stripped before applying the whitelist and before role-mapping. PR github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/842 contains unit/integration tests and a migration note. Release plan: hotfix to private control plane scheduled for 2026-03-17 during low-impact window; after rollout, revert customer whitelist change and validate nightly runs for 3 days. Follow-ups: update runbook to document namespaced-claim compatibility and add an e2e test for service-account impersonation with namespaced claims.
